title: CCT benchmark compare-config
description: Configuration consumed by `./scripts/benchmark compare --config <path>`. Lists multiple (backend, model, env) candidates to evaluate against the same benchmark task set; the harness runs them sequentially under one parent run-dir and aggregates the report.

oneOf.description: Candidate comparison — the original shape, unchanged. Scenario-only fields are forbidden here: a candidate config carrying cost_basis or trial_seeds would be silently ignored by the candidate runner, which is fail-open.

Scenario comparison (routing-eval E1). cost_basis is REQUIRED — one declared basis per comparison is normative. Candidate-only fields (candidates, runs, attempt_timeout_seconds) are forbidden; 'trials' is the scenario-side repetition field.

benchmark.description: Benchmark adapter id, as listed by `./scripts/benchmark list` (e.g. 'aider-polyglot', 'stub', 'cct-dogfood-memkernel').

runs.description: Number of repetitions per task per candidate. Higher values reduce stdev and enable the calibrated winner-declaration rule; 3 is the recommended floor for cross-LLM comparisons.

task.description: Optional task-id filter; same shape as `./scripts/benchmark run --task <id>` (repeatable). Omit to run every task the adapter exposes.

attempt_timeout_seconds.description: Optional per-attempt wall-clock timeout (seconds). Parsed and retained by `compare._validate`/`CompareConfig`, then threaded to the backend via `RunContext.timeout_seconds`. A timed-out attempt is recorded with `result='timeout'` and `scores.timeout=true`, counted as a pass_rate failure, and flagged separately in the report tally (timed_out count). Precedence: `--attempt-timeout` CLI flag > this config field > the wrapper's heuristic default (300s for cloud backends, 600s when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is non-default). Omit this field to rely on the heuristic.

candidates.description: Two or more LLM candidates to compare. Single-candidate comparisons are rejected — use `./scripts/benchmark run` for that. Each candidate runs sequentially in declaration order. Mutually exclusive with `arms`.

scenario.description: Comparison scenario id. Present only for scenario comparisons, where the unit of comparison is a ROUTING POLICY rather than a fixed (backend, model) candidate. Requires `arms`; forbidden alongside `candidates`.

arms.description: Routing-policy arms compared over the same task set, trial seeds, and injected event stream. The four mandatory kinds (always_best, always_cheapest, oracle, cct_router) must each appear exactly once — a report without its complete control set refuses to publish a cct_router figure — and oracle_budget is the only optional kind. minItems enforces the floor; the composition rule is enforced by benchmark_runner.routing_eval.scenario_config, through which the scenario driver loads every config. Mutually exclusive with 'candidates'.

cost_basis.description: The single cost provenance every cell used for cost must satisfy: 'measured' (backend-reported total_cost_usd) or 'estimated@<price-table-version>'. Mixed provenance is refused everywhere cost is used — baseline selection, the cost axis, the Pareto frontier, and oracle_budget. When cells cannot meet the declared basis the cost axis is withheld as insufficient_evidence rather than partially drawn. Scenario comparisons only.

trials.description: Trial count per (task, profile) cell for a scenario comparison. Trials are a DIMENSION of the outcome matrix, never averaged away before it is stored. A single-trial run is labelled as such and is never reported as a rate. Scenario comparisons only; `runs` remains the candidate-comparison field.

trial_seeds.description: Explicit per-trial seeds, paired across every arm so each arm sees the same trial under the same conditions. Length must equal `trials`. Part of the preset digest, so changing a seed invalidates outcome-matrix reuse. Scenario comparisons only.

event_stream.description: The deterministic provider events injected during the scenario, in order. Supplied through the documented test-only seams (CCT_SUPERVISOR_HARNESS_CMD, CCT_ROUTING_PROBE_CMD) as the CHILD's output, so the real unmodified classifier does its real work on it. Part of the preset digest. Scenario comparisons only.

budget_ceiling_usd.description: Optional PER-CELL cost ceiling enabling the oracle_budget arm. The ceiling is per-cell and only per-cell: it is asserted for every selected cell, and NO claim is made about the arm's summed cost. Global-budget allocation is out of scope. Scenario comparisons only.

tier1_only_tasks.description: The #109 Tier-1-only NEGATIVE CONTROLS: tasks whose route class pins tier1_only. The arc verifier requires their records to show a Tier-2 candidate REJECTED with the route/class reason — merely ending up on Tier-1 is insufficient, because absence is not refusal. Scenario comparisons only.

delegate_tasks.description: Tasks the scenario delegates as bounded Tier-2 packets (the #109 §12 arc's Tier-2 leg). Each must be declared in 'task', carry a tier2 route class in the worktree's routing-tasks.yaml (the supervisor refuses otherwise), and be disjoint from tier1_only_tasks. Scenario comparisons only.

kind.description: Which routing policy this arm represents. always_best / always_cheapest / oracle / oracle_budget are DERIVED from the outcome matrix. Only cct_router executes live, because its choices depend on the injected event stream and on real failure classification.

registry.description: Path to the routing registry this arm evaluates under. Required for cct_router; the derived arms read eligibility from the same registry. Its parsed digest is a component of the outcome-matrix reuse fingerprint, so any registry edit invalidates reuse.

name.description: Optional human-readable label; defaults to `kind`. Must be unique across arms.

at_task_index.description: Zero-based index into the scenario's task order at which this event is injected.

outcome.description: The provider outcome the injected child output represents. The scenario emits a transcript of this shape; the router's own unmodified classifier decides what it means. NOTE the increment-B distinction the live supervisor enforces: 'usage_limit' is the rate_limit_error ENVELOPE (Retry-After), which the action table answers with ONE same-profile retry; 'quota_exhausted' is the text-form pool exhaustion (hours-scale), which cools the profile and drives FAILOVER — the #109 §12 arc's usage-limit leg is this one.

reset_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 reset instant carried by the injected transcript, exercising the recovery-timing precedence chain. Null when the simulated provider states no reset.

retry_after_sec.description: Optional Retry-After the injected transcript carries. Null when absent.

name.description: Human-readable label for this candidate; appears in compare-manifest.json. Defaults to '<backend>:<model>'. Must be unique across all candidates; set explicitly when (backend, model) overlaps but env routing differs.

backend.description: Backend family (copilot CLI), e.g. 'claude-code', 'stub'. The deprecated combined form 'claude-code:sonnet' is rejected — split into separate backend + model fields.

model.description: Model identifier passed to the backend, e.g. 'sonnet', 'opus', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', or — when routing through a gateway — the model name the gateway serves (e.g. 'meta-llama/Llama-3-70B-Instruct'). The stub backend ignores this field.

env.description: Provider-routing env vars applied only for this candidate's runs and restored afterward. Typical keys: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL (for Claude Code's gateway support — see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway). VALUES MAY CONTAIN SECRETS and are read into os.environ for the candidate's runs; only the KEY NAMES are persisted to compare-manifest.json.
